title: UX grammar for collapsible insights and compact cost summaries
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Establish a consistent UX grammar for compact cost summary cards and their collapsible insight states across the Console. Deliver Figma components, a minimal token mapping, and usage guidelines for product teams building lightweight budget/telemetry surfaces and rollout rail integrations.
acceptance_criteria: Figma library contains compact 'cost-summary' component with 3 responsive variants: expanded, collapsed, and pinned-mini
Design tokens required for density mapping are identified and documented (spacing, type-scale, elevation, color ramps)
Prototype demonstrates collapse/expand animation <= 140ms and preserves keyboard focus and screen-reader context
Console QA validates card rendering across small (320px) to large (1440px) viewports with no visual regressions
Engineering has implementation guidance for rollout affordance (canary vs global) and graceful fallback to legacy card if token set unavailable
comments: 2026-02-22: Kickoff meeting with PM and Eng (Morgan, Diego, Lin). Agreed scope: compact cards for Cost view and Rollout rail; exclude experimental telemetry widgets from first pass.
2026-02-27: Initial Figma prototypes uploaded. Rapid iteration showed cramped text at 320px — adjusted type-scale-compact and spacing.small tokens.
2026-03-03: Accessibility review: ensured aria-expanded semantics and announced summary text when collapsed. Added high-contrast border option for color-blind use cases.
2026-03-07: Eng feedback (ENG-9201): clarified how KV-cache and streaming updates are surfaced in the mini-card; added guidance for live-update stuttering and debounce window (200ms).
2026-03-10: Design review with product: agreed on canary rollout behavior and fallback priority list (variant -> pinned-mini -> legacy-card). Action: produce rollout knob spec for Console roadmap.
2026-03-12: Submitted final Figma components and token mapping. Requesting Frontend review and token PR merge with design-tokens repo. Next: QA ticket and implementation spike.
Notes: Links above contain the interactive prototype and the spec doc with motion timings, token values, and recommended accessibility labels.
decisions: Use a 3-state compact card: expanded (default on desktop), collapsed (mobile/space-constrained), and pinned-mini (always visible small chip)
Adopt motion easing curve 'fast-out' and duration 120ms for collapse/expand to feel snappy and reduce perceived latency
Prefer single-source token mapping: map density variants to spacing.small/spacing.xsmall and type.scale-compact to avoid proliferation of new tokens
Canary rollout will be controlled at route-level with a flag; platform should fallback to 'pinned-mini' when token set is not loaded or client renders in legacy mode
next_steps: Create Frontend spike ticket to prototype token toggles and collapse animation in staging
Open QA ticket that runs component visual diffs across viewport range and color schemes
Coordinate token PR (design-tokens) and request backend flag for rollout control
Schedule dev handoff session and record short walkthrough for Platform and Solutions teams
